title: "Latent class analysis"

# Latent class analysis

LCA identifies unobserved subgroups (latent classes) from a set of categorical indicator variables. This module wraps `poLCA` to fit a sequence of models, compare them by information criteria, and assign each respondent to a class.

The helper lives in [`R/lca.R`](https://github.com/connectors-testing-pplx/research-paper-template/blob/main/R/lca.R).

## 1. Fit models with 1…K classes

```r
source("R/lca.R")

lca <- fit_lca(
  data      = analysis_df,
  indicators = c("item1", "item2", "item3", "item4", "item5"),
  max_k      = 5,
  nrep       = 10,        # random starts per model
  weights    = "wt"       # optional sampling weights
)
```

`fit_lca()` fits models with 1 through `max_k` classes and returns a tidy comparison table.

## 2. Choose the number of classes

```r
tab <- compare_classes(lca)
print(tab)               # K, AIC, BIC, entropy, % classified
plot_bic(lca)             # BIC vs K -> outputs/figures/lca-bic.png
```

A common rule of thumb: prefer the model with the lowest BIC, subject to interpretable classes and entropy above ~0.7.

## 3. Assign classes and profile them

```r
assigned <- assign_classes(lca)
profile <- class_profiles(lca)   # item-response probabilities per class
print(profile)
plot_profiles(lca)               # -> outputs/figures/lca-profiles.png
```

`assign_classes()` adds a `class` column to the data; `class_profiles()` gives the conditional probabilities that define each class for the manuscript.

## 4. Use the classes downstream

The assigned classes become a categorical variable for cross-tabs, regression, or network coloring:

```r
analysis_df$class <- assigned$class
```

## Where it plugs into the pipeline

`analysis/04-lca.R` writes `lca-classes.parquet` (the data plus class assignments) and `lca-profiles.csv` to `outputs/`, ready to cite in the results section.
